$why: A quality gate can find a change's TEST insufficient while the code is right — a mutation survives because no
assertion can tell the mutant from the original. Such a finding used to go back to the code writer, who may not
touch tests (test-ownership), committed nothing, and the phase looped. The gate-finding-analyst now judges whether
a finding is test work; when it is, the test-writer receives this section after its own prompt and strengthens the
test the change already carries. Its commit is what the gates re-run on.
A fragment composed into the repro-test-writer's prompt: no seam declares it, so it renders from the engine
layer and takes its project content from the values below.
description: Tells the test-writer that a QA gate found the change's test insufficient, and what the gate found.

bodies.prompt:
## THIS TURN: A QUALITY GATE FOUND THE TEST INSUFFICIENT
The change above is committed and its test at __TARGET_REL__ already exists and passes. The __GATE_LABEL__ gate then judged that test insufficient, and its analyst judged that the product code is right and only the test must change. This is the finding:
```json
__FINDING__
```
The gate's own report:
```
__GATE_EVIDENCE__
```
Strengthen the test at __TARGET_REL__ so that what the gate found is no longer true: add or sharpen the cases that would fail if the behaviour the finding names were broken. Keep every existing case, and keep them passing — rewrite the file in full with the existing cases and yours. Do not change any source file. Everything above about framework, typechecking and mocks still applies.
bodies.unchanged:
## YOUR PREVIOUS ATTEMPT LEFT THE TEST UNCHANGED
The file at __TARGET_REL__ is byte-for-byte what was already committed, so nothing the __GATE_LABEL__ gate found has been addressed. Add the cases the finding requires and write the file again.
